name: Browser Automation Agents
question: Should the agent read the page or look at it?
summary: Browser agents act on websites through a controlled browser. They can observe a page as screenshots, raw HTML or an accessibility tree; the tree gives roles, names and stable references in a few thousand tokens and is usually the best default, with screenshots added for visual layout. Hybrid designs script the known steps such as navigation and login in code and let the agent handle what varies, which is cheaper and more reliable than a fully autonomous agent.
useCases: Portals without APIs: regulators, exchanges, vendors

items.detail: deterministic code for what never changes
self-healing through the agent when layouts change

Script stable steps; let the agent handle the rest

steps.title: A browser you control
steps.text: Playwright runs a clean browser with no personal profile. The agent never uses anyone’s everyday browser.

steps.title: Script the fixed route
steps.text: Navigation, search and login never change from day to day, so they are plain code: fast, cheap and reliable.

steps.title: Read the accessibility tree
steps.text: A snapshot lists roles, names and links in about 3,000 tokens, against about 25,000 for raw HTML.

steps.title: The agent decides what varies
steps.text: Only the judgement goes to the model: which notice is today’s corporate action. It answers with a role and a name.

steps.title: Stay on the allowlist
steps.text: Before following a link, the code checks the domain. A link to an unknown site is refused.

steps.title: Extract into a schema
steps.text: The notice becomes a typed record, such as record date and ratio, validated before it reaches the system.

practice.scenario: A fictional broker’s operations team checked corporate-action notices on exchange and registrar websites every morning. A fully autonomous browser agent working from screenshots and raw HTML was slow and cost about 25,000 tokens a page. The rebuilt agent scripts navigation and login in Playwright, reads each page as an accessibility snapshot of about 3,000 tokens, and only decides which notice to open and what it says. It finishes in a third of the time.

industries.use: Corporate actions, circulars and filings from exchange sites
Downloading statements and bureau reports from portals

practice.analogy: A new analyst with a checklist: the routine route to the page is written down step by step, and judgement is spent only on reading what is there.

library.name: Playwright
library.what: A controlled browser; aria_snapshot() gives a compact accessibility tree the model can read, and get_by_role() acts on what it chooses.
library.install: pip install playwright && playwright install chromium

practice.note: Site structure and labels change; keep the scripted part small and let the agent handle what varies. Respect each site’s terms of use.

samples.code:
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

ALLOWED = ("www.nseindia.com", "www.bseindia.com")

def todays_notices(llm, company: str):
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch()
        page = browser.new_page()
        page.goto("https://www.bseindia.com/corporates/ann.html")   # scripted step
        page.get_by_role("textbox", name="Security Name").fill(company)
        page.get_by_role("button", name="Submit").click()

        tree = page.locator("body").aria_snapshot()                # ~3k tokens
        choice = llm.pick_link(tree, goal=f"today's corporate actions for {company}")
        link = page.get_by_role("link", name=choice.name)
        assert link.get_attribute("href").split("/")[2] in ALLOWED, "off-allowlist"
        link.click()

        summary = llm.extract(page.locator("main").aria_snapshot(),
                              schema=CorporateAction)               # structured output
        browser.close()
        return summary

numericDrill.question: A browser agent reads 12 pages per task. Raw HTML costs about 25,000 tokens a page and an accessibility snapshot about 3,000. At ₹0.25 per 1,000 input tokens, how much does switching save per task, in ₹?
numericDrill.answer: 12 × (25,000 − 3,000) = 264,000 tokens; 264 × ₹0.25 = ₹66 saved per task. The snapshot is also easier for the model to act on, because it names roles and elements instead of burying them in markup.

interview.question: Screenshot, HTML or accessibility tree: which should a browser agent observe?
interview.answer: Usually the accessibility tree: it is compact, lists roles and names, and gives stable references to act on. Add screenshots where layout or visuals matter, such as charts or canvases. Raw HTML is complete but large and noisy, and wastes context.

interview.question: Why script parts of a browser workflow instead of letting the agent do everything?
interview.answer: Steps that never change, such as navigation and login, are faster, cheaper and more reliable in code. Letting the agent handle only what varies, such as finding the right notice or reading its contents, reduces errors and cost and keeps the flow auditable.

mistakes.mistake: A fully autonomous agent for a fixed route
mistakes.fix: Script the fixed steps, use the agent for judgement
